title: docs(spec): correct the stale `cloud/environment.zod.ts` attribution in the discovery-environment subset pin
body:
Fixes #17730

Clause-②: no

The pin test's docblock told a reader that `EnvironmentTypeSchema` is declared by `cloud/environment.zod.ts`, while the file's own import 28 lines below reads `./discovery.zod`. Class (b): a declared statement contradicted by measurable behaviour in the same file. Only prose moves here — no schema, no assertion, no assertion message.

## Premise, re-verified first-hand on `origin/main` (not taken from the card)

```
git ls-tree -d origin/main packages/spec/src/cloud   ->  (no output: ABSENT)
git ls-tree -d origin/main packages/spec/src/api     ->  040000 tree 61d3b3d7…   (lit control: the instrument prints a tree when one exists)
git grep -n 'EnvironmentTypeSchema *=' origin/main -- 'packages/spec/src/**'
     ->  packages/spec/src/api/discovery.zod.ts:434
```

Deletion traced to a commit, with a firing control:

```
git log --diff-filter=D -- packages/spec/src/cloud/environment.zod.ts
  ->  776d64cd3d  2026-09-10  feat(spec)!: drop the `@objectstack/spec/cloud` subpath … (#17372)
      commit body: "`EnvironmentType` is re-declared in `api/discovery.zod.ts`"
control (a file that still exists, same command):
git log --diff-filter=D -- packages/spec/src/api/discovery.zod.ts   ->  (empty, as it must be)
```

So `#16325` is the ruling and `#17372` / `776d64cd3d` is the landing. The in-tree prose at `api/discovery.zod.ts:412` already attributes the move to `#16325` ("Until #16325 this enum was declared by `cloud/environment.zod.ts`"), and this docblock now matches that convention.

Line numbers were taken off the tree, not off the card: the card says the import is at `:39` and the second residue at `:27-28`; on `origin/main` @ `5ed7ad9df8` they are at `:40` and `:26-27`.

## What changed — two residues, both in the docblock

1. **The declaration table row** (`:12`) now names `api/discovery.zod.ts`. One sentence is added below the table recording why both rows name one module, so the repetition does not read as a copy-paste slip and does not get "repaired" back.
2. **The reverse cross-reference note** (`:26-27`) named the two carrier FILES, one of which no longer exists. It now names the two DECLARATIONS — which is what that sentence is actually about, and what survives the next move.

Both cross-reference claims were re-derived rather than copied forward:

| claim | verified |
|:---|:---|
| `DiscoveryEnvironmentSchema`'s `.describe()` since #4828 | `git log -S'a richer 7-member taxonomy'` -> `77022a99ce` = #4828 (PR #5682) |
| `EnvironmentTypeSchema`'s JSDoc since this pin | `git log --diff-filter=A` on the pin file -> `0261016601` (PR #6288), the same commit that introduced the reverse citation; carried into `api/discovery.zod.ts` by `776d64cd3d` |

## The member lists were re-derived, not copied forward

The table's factual claim about each enum's vocabulary is **correct** and is unchanged by this PR:

- `DiscoveryEnvironmentSchema` (`discovery.zod.ts:473`) = `production` `sandbox` `development` — 3.
- `EnvironmentTypeSchema` (`discovery.zod.ts:434`) = those three plus `test` `staging` `preview` `trial` — 7.

The two folds the docblock cites also hold against `NODE_ENV_TO_DISCOVERY_ENVIRONMENT` (`discovery.zod.ts:591`): `staging` -> `sandbox`, `test` -> `development`.

## Tests and gates

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --project local src/api/discovery-environment-subset.pin.test.ts` — **4 passed**, VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — **483 files / 13775 tests passed**, VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` — exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit` + `check:scripts-typecheck` + `check:test-typecheck`; the last compiles the test layer under `tsconfig.test.json`, which is what reaches this file).
- Dependency closure: `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/spec^...' build` -> "No projects matched the filters" — `packages/spec` has no workspace dependencies, so step 1 is an empty run. `packages/spec` itself was built before every `dist/`-reading gate, and later `pnpm build` (73/73 tasks successful) before the four gates that refuse without one.
- Derived gate families: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` -> 78 commands, each run with its exit code landed to disk before any pipe, reconciled with `--ran`: **78 derived, 78 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN** (reconciler exit 0).
- 77 of the 78 are green. The one red is `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` (exit 1), and it is the **known, already-filed** local-only signature: it flags `@objectstack/cli` descending `packages/spec/dist/`, which exists only on a tree where `packages/spec` has been built — cards #18353 / #18440. Not re-filed, and not caused by this diff.
- `pnpm lint` equivalent, run whole rather than narrowed: `eslint . --no-inline-config --format json` over the repo -> **6803 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings**, exit 0. The population figure is eslint's own count from its `--format json` output, not an estimate.
- Control characters: `grep -naP` over the changed file finds none, and `pnpm check:nul-bytes` is green.

## Changeset — `skip-changeset`, measured

`packages/spec`'s `files[]` is `dist · json-schema · liveness · prompts · llms.txt · README.md · src/**/*.zod.ts · CHANGELOG.md · api-surface · spec-changes.json`. After a full build, grepping every one of those paths:

- the text this PR adds: **0 hits** in the published paths, **0 hits** in `src/**/*.zod.ts`;
- positive control `EnvironmentTypeSchema`: **12 files** in the published paths, **1** in `src/**/*.zod.ts` — the instrument fires;
- a `.pin.test.ts` is not a `*.zod.ts` and nothing named `pin` is emitted into `dist/`.

A comment inside a test file publishes nothing from any released package, so `skip-changeset` is the right label and `patch` would be wrong.

## Acceptance notes

Noted, not folded in — the same `#16325` root, one line **inside the test body**, which this card's dispatch explicitly ring-fences ("do not change what the test asserts"):

`:61` of the same file, in the failure message of the second assertion, reads "if a bucket was renamed on **the cloud side**, rename it here". Post-#16325 the enum is declared here, in the open-source spec, so as a statement about *where a rename happens* it is stale. It is also arguably still true as a statement about *where a rename originates* — the `sys_environment` row and its taxonomy remain the cloud control plane's, and `DiscoveryEnvironmentSchema`'s own `.describe()` still says "that is `sys_environment` / EnvironmentTypeSchema". Ambiguous enough that it is a reading for the seat, not a silent edit in a prose-only PR. Reported, not filed by this seat.
